title: Rotate a Chain Right
statement:
You get the head of a singly linked list and a non-negative integer k. Rotate the list to the right by k places: one rotation takes the last node off the end and puts it at the front.

Return the head of the rotated list. k can be much larger than the list's length. The list may be empty.

In tests a list is written as an array of its values, from head to tail.

examples.why: The last two nodes move to the front, keeping their order.
Every 3 rotations bring the list back to where it started, so 7 rotations act like 7 mod 3 = 1. Rotating 7 times one by one works but wastes time; with k = 2·10⁹ it is hopeless.
k equals the length, so the list is unchanged.

hints: Rotating by the length of the list changes nothing. So which k actually matters?
After reducing k modulo the length n, the new head is the node at position n − k from the start, and the node before it becomes the new tail.
Find the length and the tail in one walk, link the tail to the head to form a ring, walk n − k steps from the tail, and cut the ring there.

explain.intuition:
Rotating by n, the length, gives back the original list, so only k mod n matters. After that, rotating right by k means the last k nodes move to the front as one block. The list is cut in exactly one place: after node number n − k.

A neat way to do the surgery: walk to the tail (counting n on the way) and connect it to the head, which makes a ring. Now walk n − k steps from the old tail; that node is the new tail, its next is the new head, and you break the ring there.
steps: If the list is empty, return it.
Walk to the tail and count the length n.
Set k = k mod n. If k is 0, return the head unchanged.
Link tail.next = head to close a ring.
From the tail, step forward n − k times to reach the new tail. Set newHead = newTail.next, cut with newTail.next = null, and return newHead.
pitfalls: Rotating one step at a time, k times. With k up to 2·10⁹ that never finishes.
Taking k mod n before checking for an empty list, which divides by zero.
Forgetting to cut the ring, which returns a list that loops forever.

solutions.title: Copy values, rotate the array, rebuild
solutions.idea: Read the values into an array, slice it at n − k, and build a new list.

solutions.title: Close the ring, then cut it
solutions.idea: Count the length, link the tail to the head, walk n − (k mod n) steps from the tail, and cut.

followups: Rotate to the left by k instead. Which single number changes?
Rotate an array in place by k with O(1) extra space. How do three reversals do it?
